definition: Generative AI pornography, is pornographic content that is produced uses generative AI technology.
details: It may include, allusions towards animation, literature, video games, and other forms of popular culture. The content may depict softcore pornography, including lascivious behavior, or more explicit material depicting sexual intercourse and erotic art. Such material may be original characters, or real people through deepfakes.

explainer.lead: Generative AI pornography is sexually explicit material created by systems that generate new images or other media. It matters because the same technology can depict fictional characters or place real people in sexual content without their consent, raising difficult questions about harm, consent, and regulation.

tiers.eli5: Some computer programs can make pictures from written instructions, like a drawing machine that follows a description. People can use these programs to make sexual pictures of invented characters, but they can also misuse them to make sexual images of real people without permission. That can seriously hurt the person shown, even when the image itself is fake.
tiers.practitioner: Applications typically expose text prompts or feature selectors for appearance, clothing, demographic traits, and style, often alongside iterative editing, galleries, and prompt enhancement; some also produce short clips or configurable interactive characters. Stable Diffusion is a prominent open-source tool, while dedicated sites wrap various generative models. Practical risks include non-consensual likenesses, deepfake and nudifier misuse, stereotypes inherited from training material, and weak or bypassable safeguards in local models.
tiers.paperLevel: In plain-text notation, generated content can be represented as y = G(c), where G is a generative model and c encodes prompts, selected attributes, style, or optional reference material; deepfake pornography instead alters existing content depicting a person. Stable Diffusion, an open-source text-to-image model using LAION-5B, is associated with the technology's early-2020s spread. Open problems include consent for training likenesses and voices, stereotyped outputs, child-abuse-material risks, safeguard bypasses, and legal frameworks that address non-consensual deepfakes more directly than wholly synthesized content.

explainer.example: A user selects an anime style, describes a fictional adult character, and then revises the prompt and edits the generated image. If the user instead mapped a celebrity's face onto sexual imagery, that would be deepfake pornography involving a real person's likeness.

explainer.intuition: A generative model uses patterns learned from training data to turn a description or selected traits into new sexual content. The result may be synthesized around an original character, or it may incorporate a real person's likeness through techniques such as deepfakes or face morphing.
howItWorks: A user supplies a text prompt, selects visual traits, or uploads material as a starting point.
A generative model produces an image, short video, GIF, or configurable interactive character.
The user can adjust settings, style, or theme, then refine prompts and edit earlier outputs.
Optional nudifier, deepfake, or face-morphing tools alter existing material or introduce a person's likeness.
Platforms may publish results in categorized galleries that others can browse or modify.
explainer.whyItMatters: Non-consensual outputs can enable harassment, blackmail, or revenge porn, while training on people's voices or likenesses raises separate consent concerns. Using existing pornography as training material may also reinforce harmful stereotypes, and current laws more often target deepfakes of real people than fully synthesized material.
misconceptions: Not all AI-generated pornography is a deepfake: deepfakes alter existing content, while other outputs are synthesized from scratch.
Using a fictional character does not remove every ethical issue, including training-data consent, stereotyping, and possible child-abuse material.
Restrictions in proprietary services do not prevent misuse through local open-source models or bypassed safeguards.
